Replacing a married couple's Social Security income with dividends sounds straightforward until you see how brutally the math punishes the wrong yield tier at the wrong time in retirement.
Two investors hold the exact same dividend ETF and receive identical distributions, yet one quietly hands thousands more to the IRS each year. The account they chose made all the difference.

Most investors chasing high dividend yields are quietly funding their own losses without realizing it. Before you build a retirement income portfolio, there are three yield tiers worth understanding, and the math behind them changes everything about how much capital you actually need.
One covered call ETF turns a fixed pool of retirement savings into a monthly paycheck, but the yield that makes it work also quietly sets a trap most retirees spot too late.

Five options-income ETFs are quietly paying two to three times the 10-year Treasury rate every single month, but the machinery underneath each fund is radically different, and picking the wrong one for your situation costs you more than you might expect.
